parole.significato: Brahmin
parole.testo: Borrowed from Punjabi ਬਾਹਮਣ (bāhmaṇ) / باہْمَݨ (bāhmaṇ). Doublet of Brahmin and Brahman.

parole.significato: A holy man in Sikhism or Hinduism.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Punjabi ਭਗਤ (bhagat), from Sanskrit भक्त (bhakta). Doublet of bhakt.

parole.significato: A lively style of music originating from India.
parole.testo: From Punjabi ਭੰਗੜਾ (bhaṅgṛā) / بَھن٘گْڑا (bhaṉgṛā), from ਭੰਗ / بَھن٘گ (bhaṉg, “hemp”) + ـڑا (-ṛā).

parole.significato: a slur, usually but not always casteist, which emerged after Partition and has different connotations depending on the…
parole.testo: From Punjabi ਭਾਪਾ (bhāpā, “father, elder brother”). The term originated in the Potohari dialect of Punjabi spoken around Rawalpindi, and was brought to India by Sikhs, particularly of Khatri background, who fled the 1947 Rawalpindi massacres which occurred prior to Partition. parole.significato: scrambled
parole.testo: Borrowed from Punjabi ਭੁਰਜੀ (bhurjī), ultimately from Sanskrit भृज्जति (bhṛjjati, “roasts, fries”). Related to fry and bhujia.

parole.significato: Heroin.
parole.testo: From Punjabi ਚਿੱਟਾ (ciṭṭā).

parole.significato: Synonym of dupatta – a long scarf worn by South Asian women.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Punjabi چُنّی (cunnī) / Punjabi ਚੁੰਨੀ (cunnī).

parole.significato: A pair of tight-fitting trousers, worn by men and women in South Asia.
parole.testo: From Punjabi ਚੂੜੀਦਾਰ (cūṛīdār).

parole.significato: A turban worn by Sikhs.
parole.testo: From Punjabi دستار / ਦਸਤਾਰ (dastār), from Classical Persian دستار (dastār).

parole.significato: A bowed string instrument of Indian origin, with a goatskin soundboard, sympathetic strings attached to a sitar-like ne…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Punjabi ਇਸਰਾਜ (isarāj).

parole.significato: A traditional South Asian form of combat training in which wooden sticks are used to simulate swords in sparring matche…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Punjabi ਗਤਕਾ (gatkā).

parole.significato: The person who reads the sacred scripture at a Sikh religious ceremony.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Punjabi ਗ੍ਰੰਥੀ (granthī).

parole.significato: a term used to refer to compositions by Sikh gurus
parole.testo: Borrowed from Punjabi ਗੁਰਬਾਣੀ (gurbāṇī).

parole.significato: A Sikh place of worship.
parole.testo: From Punjabi ਗੁਰਦੁਆਰਾ (gurduārā), ਗੁਰਦਵਾਰਾ (gurdavārā).

parole.significato: Alternate form of Jat, primarily used by Eastern Punjabi groups, particularly Sikhs.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Punjabi ਜੱਟ (jaṭṭ). See ਜੱਟ (jaṭṭ) or Jat for more.

parole.significato: The instant decapitation method of animal slaughter, idealized as a non-ritual alternative to ritual slaughter (kutha)…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Punjabi ਝਟਕਾ (jhaṭkā, “sudden movement, jerking”) / جَھٹْکا (jhaṭkā). Unrelated to Slovak jatka (“slaugherhouse”) or Polish jatka (“butchershop”).

parole.significato: An item of footwear embroidered with silver or gold thread.
parole.testo: From Punjabi ਜੁੱਤੀ (juttī).

parole.significato: An undergarment worn by baptized Sikhs, one of the five Ks.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Punjabi ਕਛੈਰਾ (kachairā).

parole.significato: A comb, required to be worn at all times by Sikhs, one of the five Ks.
parole.testo: From Punjabi ਕੰਘਾ (kaṅghā).

parole.significato: A bangle worn by Sikhs, one of the five Ks, to remind them to do God's work.
parole.testo: From Punjabi ਕੜਾ (kaṛā); see Hindi कड़ा (kaṛā, “bracelet”).

parole.significato: Related to Khalistan, a name for the Punjab region of northern India.
parole.testo: From Khalistan + -i. Derived from Punjabi ਖ਼ਾਲਿਸਤਾਨ (xālistān, literally “place of Khalsa”).

parole.significato: Baptized Sikhs, taken collectively.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Punjabi ਖ਼ਾਲਸਾ (xālsā) / خالْصَہ (xālṣah), ultimately from Arabic خَالِص (ḵāliṣ, “pure”).

parole.significato: A double-edged sword from India, used ceremonially in Sikhism.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Punjabi ਖੰਡਾ (khaṇḍā), from Sanskrit खड्ग (khaḍga).

parole.significato: A member of the second-highest of the four castes or varnas in traditional Punjabi society.
parole.testo: From Punjabi ਖਤਰੀ (khatrī), Hindi खत्री (khatrī), Nepali खत्री (khatrī).

parole.significato: A ceremonial sword that must be worn at all times by baptized Sikhs, and one of the five Ks.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Punjabi ਕਿਰਪਾਨ (kirpān), from Sanskrit कृपाण (kṛpāṇa, “sword, dagger, sacrificial knife”), from कल्पयति (kalpáyati, “he orders, apportions, cuts, trims”).

parole.significato: A type of leavened bread from northern India, made with wheat flour and usually eaten with chole.
parole.testo: From Punjabi ਕੁਲਚਾ (kulcā), from Classical Persian کلیچه (kulīča), کلچه (kolča). Doublet of kulich.

parole.significato: Relating to Lahore.
parole.testo: From Punjabi لَہَوری (lahaurī); which means "of Lahore" from Lahore, a city in Punjab, Pakistan. Equivalent to Lahore + -i.

parole.significato: Cooked Punjabi-style in a rich sauce containing butter, tomatoes and cream.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Punjabi ਮੱਖਣੀ (makkhaṇī) or Hindi मखनी (makhnī, “buttery”).

parole.significato: A type of raised bed similar to a cot from South Asia.
parole.testo: From a form of Punjabi ਮੰਜਾ (mañjā, “raised bed”). The Sikh sense is based on their use as seats of authority.

parole.significato: Any of the twelve sovereign states in the Sikh Confederacy that rose during the eighteenth century in the Punjab.
parole.testo: From Punjabi ਮਿਸਲ (misal).

parole.significato: Attachment to the transient material world, which hinders the soul's search for its ultimate goal and is therefore one…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Punjabi ਮੋਹ (moh), itself borrowed from Sanskrit मोह (moha).

parole.significato: A Sikh holy flag, colored orange and white, with a symbol of the khanda.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Punjabi ਨਿਸ਼ਾਨ ਸਾਹਿਬ (niśān sāhib, literally “respected ensign”), from ਨਿਸ਼ਾਨ (niśān, “sign, mark”) + ਸਾਹਿਬ (sāhib, “owner, master; term of respect”).

parole.significato: A person of South Asian ancestry.
parole.testo: An invented Indian-sounding given name, originating from the Pajeet, my son meme created on the 4chan message board /int/ in July 2015, mocking South Asians. This was itself inspired by the Mehmet, my son meme, popularized on /int/ in late 2014, which mocked Turkish people. Although the name does no

parole.significato: A head covering worn by Sikh boys, and by Sikh men either alone or as an under-turban.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Punjabi ਪਟਕਾ (paṭkā) and/or Hindi पटका (paṭkā). Doublet of purdah.

parole.significato: Relating to Peshawar.
parole.testo: From Punjabi پِشَوری (piśaurī); which means "of Peshawar" from Peshawar, a city in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan.

parole.significato: A style of Punjabi embroidery characterized by patterns of flowers.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Punjabi ਫੁਲਕਾਰੀ (phulkārī).

parole.significato: A volunteer who offers his or her help to a gurdwara or to the community, for religious reasons.
parole.testo: From Punjabi ਸੇਵਾਦਾਰ (sevādār, “attendant, servant”).

parole.significato: A weapon.
parole.testo: Punjabi [Term?]

parole.significato: An adherent of Sikhism.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Punjabi ਸਿੱਖ (sikkha).

parole.significato: A Muslim man; especially one from Pakistan.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Punjabi ਸੁੱਲਾ (sullā, “Muslim (derogatory)”). This word is likely a mispronunciation (or perhaps a misspelling in Gurmukhi script) of Punjabi ਮੁੱਲਾ (mullā, “mullah, Islamic religious leader”), derived from Classical Persian ملا (mullā), ultimately from Arabic مُلَّا (mullā). It may als

parole.significato: A traditional North Indian musical instrument from Punjab with a single string.
parole.testo: From Punjabi ਤੂੰਬੀ (tūmbī).

parole.significato: A bearded reddish sheep, subspecies of Ovis orientalis (including Ovis orientalis vignei), previously classified as Ovi…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Pothohari Punjabi ہڑیال m (huṛiāl), ultimately from Sanskrit हुड m (huḍa).

parole.significato: a Sikh living in the Sikh diaspora, especially one from the West
parole.testo: From Punjabi ਯੱਕਾ (yakkā), usually referring to an ace (a type of playing card) or a horse-drawn cart, but can also be translated into the English expletive fuck. However, the slang usage of the term is said to be a corruption of Yankee.

parole.significato: A storage room or armoury where firearms and magazines are kept.
parole.testo: From arms + possibly Punjabi ਕੋਟ (koṭ, “fort”) or Hindustani کوٹ / कोट (koṭ, “fort, barracks”), ultimately from Proto-Dravidian *kōṭṭay (“wall”). Compare Tamil கோட்டை (kōṭṭai, “fort, castle, stronghold”). Alternatively, from Hindi कोठा (koṭhā, “warehouse”) or a related cognate. First used in British

parole.significato: A fluffy deep-fried leavened bread from the Indian subcontinent.
parole.testo: From Hindi भटूरा (bhaṭūrā) or Punjabi ਭਟੂਰਾ (bhaṭūrā).
